Plot sampler diagnostics and grid diagnostics

Source: R/plot-diagnostics.R
plot_diagnostics.Rd

plot_diagnostics() plots the diagnostics returned by diagnose(): R-hat and the bulk and tail effective sample sizes (ESS) of the monitored quantities against their thresholds, and two diagnostics of the grid. The caption gives the number of divergent transitions, the number of iterations that reached the maximum tree depth, and the smallest E-BFMI.

Usage

plot_diagnostics(x, what = c("rhat", "ess", "grid"), by_block = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

what

Character vector with the diagnostics to plot: one or more of "rhat", "ess" and "grid". By default all three are plotted.

by_block

If TRUE (the default), the quantities are grouped into blocks as described in Details. If FALSE, they are shown in a single row.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

By default the monitored quantities are grouped into blocks: the spline coefficients alpha, the precision lambda, the mean, variance and standard deviation of \(g\), log_g at the grid points, the site-level quantities (if the fit stores them, see site_draws in bayes_efron_fit()), and all other quantities. A block of up to 30 quantities is shown as points. A larger block is shown as a box plot, with its worst value as a point. A name next to a block identifies its worst quantity, i.e., the one with the largest R-hat or the smallest effective sample size.

Dashed lines mark the thresholds used by diagnose(): 1.01 for R-hat and 400 for the effective sample sizes. A dotted line marks an R-hat of 1.05, above which the draws should not be used.

Sampler diagnostics are computed from all iterations of the run, even if the fit was thinned (thin) and stores only some of them. The two grid panels are computed from the stored draws.

Sampler checks that failed or were skipped are listed in the caption. For a short run (fewer than 400 draws), diagnose() skips the checks of R-hat and of the effective sample sizes. Their values are still plotted against the thresholds, but a value beyond a threshold then does not mean that a check failed. Values that are not available are not plotted, and the caption names the quantities concerned (a long list is abbreviated). This includes a quantity with an infinite R-hat: its value is stored as NA, and the caption also reports it as a failed check.

If what includes "grid", two more panels show the grid diagnostics. The first gives, for each end of the grid (its lower and upper limit), the largest posterior mass that any site has in the outer 2% of the range, and names that site. A value above the dashed line (0.05) means that the site has substantial posterior mass at that limit. The second panel compares the posterior interval of the standard deviation of \(g\) with its prior interval on the same grid. See the Details of diagnose() for how to read both panels.

See also

diagnose(), plot_mcmc(), vignette("diagnostics")

Examples

plot_diagnostics(krw_fit)


# R-hat alone, without blocks.
plot_diagnostics(twin_towers_fit, what = "rhat", by_block = FALSE)
